chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the turban for the deceased.
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Wrap it (around his head).'

key_terms.الْعِمَامَةِ: The turban or headgear worn by men, often used as a sign of respect or religious identity.
key_terms.حَنِّكْهُ: Wrap it around him (imperative form, referring to wrapping the turban around the head).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on placing a turban on the deceased in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of adorning the deceased with a turban (imamah) as part of the ritual preparation for burial, reflecting the Shia emphasis on dignifying the body in accordance with the Prophet's practice. It highlights the continuity of prophetic traditions in funeral rites, where the turban symbolizes honor and readiness for the afterlife, a practice widely accepted across Shia juristic schools.
